summary: Updates RFC 2026 to stop using STD 1 as a summary of Internet Official Protocol Standards. It obsoletes RFC 5000 and asks the IESG to move RFC 5000 and STD 1 to Historic status.

plainLanguage.summary: A yearly list was stopped because a website does the job.

subtitle: The IETF stops maintaining the Internet Official Protocol Standards list known as STD 1.

tldr.problem: RFC 2026 required a periodically published summary of the status of all Internet protocol specifications (STD 1, by then RFC 5000), but it had not been kept up to date and people used the RFC Editor's online list instead.
tldr.mechanism: This BCP removes the three paragraphs in RFC 2026 that call for the summary, obsoletes RFC 5000, and asks the IESG to move RFC 5000 and STD 1 to Historic status.
tldr.outcome: The online list from the RFC Editor is the place to look for status, and IESG minutes are the publication of record for standards actions.

today: RFC 7100 is a Best Current Practice and, per the unit metadata, has not been obsoleted or updated. It obsoletes RFC 5000 and updates RFC 2026.

sections.title: Why STD 1 Is Retired
sections.content:
RFC 2026 and its predecessors called for the RFC Editor to publish an "Internet Official Protocol Standards" RFC summarizing the status of all Internet protocol and service specifications. That document, by now RFC 5000, was always listed in the Internet Standard series as STD 1.

The RFC says it had not been kept up to date in recent years and had fallen out of use in favor of the online list produced by the RFC Editor. The IETF no longer saw the need to maintain it.
sections.plainLanguage: There was a big paper list of every rule and how finished it was. Nobody updated it anymore, and a website kept the same list fresh, so the paper list was not needed.

sections.title: What Changes in RFC 2026
sections.content:
This BCP updates RFC 2026 by effectively removing three paragraphs that mention the summary: one in Section 2.1, one in Section 3.3 (which says the document lists a general requirement level for each technical specification) and one in Section 6.1.3.

It also obsoletes RFC 5000 and requests that the IESG move that document, and therefore STD 1, to Historic status.

Section 6.1.3 of RFC 2026 also called for an official summary of standards actions, completed and pending, in the Internet Society's newsletter. That had not been done in recent years either. The publication of record for standards actions had for some time been the IESG minutes, so that paragraph is removed as well.
sections.plainLanguage: The rule book had a few sentences saying to keep the list. Those sentences are crossed out, and the list itself is retired.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document states only that it does not impact the security of the Internet. It is a process change and defines no protocol behavior.
sections.plainLanguage: Crossing a list off the to-do pile does not make anything less safe.

references.text: Bradner, S., "The Internet Standards Process -- Revision 3", BCP 9, RFC 2026, October 1996.
RFC Editor, "Internet Official Protocol Standards", RFC 5000, May 2008.
